notes: REPLACES AN AMOSTOOLS STUB. Until 2026-08-12 this row held only the token table with the library stripped out from under it -- both length fields zero, no code, every routine word overwritten with `====` -- so the tier could not rise above `manual`. The real library's table is IDENTICAL to the stub's, entry for entry, id for id and spec for spec, which is a check on the AMOSTools reader as much as on this registration. What changes is that the code is now here to read. Six named keywords -- `Thx Play`, `Thx Stop`, `Thx Load`, `Thx Volume`, `=Thx Subsongs`, `Thx End` -- and a seventh unnamed entry, which is routine 0's default that every extension has. THE KEYWORDS ARE THE SMALL HALF OF THE JOB. THX (The Player / AHX, by Dexter and Pink) is a SYNTHESISED chiptune format: a song is a few hundred bytes because the instruments are generated rather than sampled. Nothing in src/amiga replays it, and writing one is the same shape of problem protracker.ts was. The archive ships NINE REAL SONGS in example/songs/ -- Back in 1986, Commando-Highscore, Drums, Extra, Hawkeye-Loader, Inside, Raider of the Daim, Sometimes, Urban Shuffle, 352 to 3,312 bytes -- which is a better starting position than ProTracker had. example/THXLib_Example.AMOS shows the keywords in use. DME 2.0 also carries a `thx *` block, sharing all six names and NOT ONE id with this table, so a program written for one detokenises to nonsense under the other. CAUTION when quoting THXLib.guide: it is one of the four documents behind the nine unbalanced quotations in status.ts NOTES.
